capabilities: Expand trigger tags into inline field templates
Move between fields with Tab and suggest choices and earlier values
Search entries and insert citations or links
Show a schema's entries in a sortable, editable table
Promote an entry line to its own note
disambiguation: Not a JSON or data-schema validator; it expands tags into inline field templates inside notes.
extras: Part of the author's DoomEsque offline suite; the README states the plugin makes no network requests and that an offline audit script checks the source, bundle and styles. Beta installs go through BRAT.
motivation: Built as part of a plugin suite the author made to be certain there are no network calls, so Obsidian could be used for notes in open-book law exams.
problem: Obsidian tags are flat labels, so there is no quick way to turn a tag into a record with fixed fields that can later be searched, tabulated or made into a note.

relations.evidence: It brings Logseq-style "tags as classes" to Obsidian.
Entries are plain [key:: value] inline fields, which Dataview and Pomodoro Flashcards also read.
or when Inline Autocomplete completes it, including on list lines

summary: Turns trigger tags like #case-law into inline field templates with the cursor in the first field, then searches, tabulates and promotes those entries.
